big_picture_notes: The Book of Ezekiel is structurally one of the most meticulously organized books in the Old Testament, characterized by precise dating formulas and a chiastic literary framework. The book's overall structure is tripartite: (I) Oracles of Judgment against Judah and Jerusalem (Chapters 1-24), (II) Oracles of Judgment against Foreign Nations (Chapters 25-32), and (III) Oracles of Salvation and Restoration for Israel (Chapters 33-48). This structure is held together by the central theme of the kavod (glory) of Yahweh, which is seen departing from the Temple in the first section (Chapters 8-11) and returning to the new Temple in the final vision (Chapters 43-44), forming a massive inclusio. Major literary devices include highly detailed visionary descriptions, symbolic actions (mophetim) performed by the prophet, and the constant repetition of the recognition formula: 'Then they will know that I am the LORD.' The narrative moves with relentless chronological precision, marked by dates that place the oracles in the context of the Babylonian exile. The book's literary movement is a dramatic arc from divine abandonment and catastrophic judgment to national revival and eschatological perfection, all based on the covenantal principle of divine justice and restoration.

stories.story_title: The Chariot Vision and the Watchman's Call
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: The inaugural merkabah (chariot-throne) theophany by the River Kebar and Ezekiel's commissioning. Start (1:1): the date formula and opened heavens. End (3:27): the terms of his coming silence and speech. Glue: the divine glory (kabod), the epithet 'son of man,' and the dialogue between the prophet and the voice.

scenes.scene_name: The Heavens Opened by the Kebar
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The date formula: among the exiles, the heavens open and the word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel the priest.
A whirlwind from the north and the gleaming amber-fire creatures with human form and calf-like hooves.

scenes.scene_name: Four Faces: Man, Lion, Ox, Eagle
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The fourfold faces and outstretched wings of each creature.
Movement wherever the spirit goes, with glowing coals and fire flashing between them.
The beryl wheels beside the creatures, multidirectional, their rims full of eyes.
The wheels rising and moving in perfect unison with the living creatures.
The crystal expanse above and the thunderous roar of their wings like the voice of the Almighty.
The sapphire throne and the man-like figure of fire and rainbow brilliance — 'I fell facedown.'
The Spirit setting the prophet on his feet, sent to a rebellious nation.

scenes.scene_name: They Will Know a Prophet Was Among Them
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The commission to the obstinate children whether they listen or refuse.

scenes.scene_name: Do Not Be Afraid of Their Words
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The charge not to fear the briers, thorns, and scorpions of a rebellious house.
The outstretched hand and the scroll written front and back with mourning and woe.
The ingested scroll of doom that tastes 'as sweet as honey.'

scenes.scene_name: Not to a People of Strange Speech
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Sent to Israel, who would be harder to reach than any foreign tongue.
Israel's hard-headed refusal met by a prophet made harder than flint.
The charge to receive the words and speak to the exiles.

scenes.scene_name: Blessed Be the Glory of the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The Spirit lifting him amid the rumbling of the creatures' wings and wheels.
Carried in bitterness to Tel-abib, sitting overwhelmed for seven days.

scenes.scene_name: A Watchman for the House of Israel
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The watchman's blood-responsibility to warn the wicked.
The accountability when a righteous man turns to sin.
The glory in the plain and the command to withdraw.
Tied with ropes and his tongue silenced until God opens his mouth.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Four bizarre physical sign-acts simulating Jerusalem's siege (the brick, the side-lying, the rationed bread, the shaved hair), interpreted by the oracles against the mountains (6) and 'the End' (7). Glue: the siege/famine imagery and the nearing 'day' and 'end,' sealed by the recognition formula 'they shall know that I am the LORD.'

scenes.scene_name: The Brick and the Iron Plate
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The sign-act of besieging an engraved brick behind an iron wall — a sign to Israel.
Lying on each side to bear the iniquity of Israel and Judah by counted days.
Arm bared and tied with ropes until the days of the siege are finished.

scenes.scene_name: Bread by Weight, Water by Measure
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The mixed-grain rationing of siege famine.
The bread baked over excrement as a sign of unclean exile.
Ezekiel's priestly protest and God's concession.

scenes.scene_name: The Staff of Bread Cut Off
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Jerusalem to waste away in rationed anxiety and despair.

scenes.scene_name: The Razor and the Divided Hair
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The shaved head and beard divided in thirds — burned, struck, and scattered.
The remnant secured in the garment, yet even some of those burned.
The city set among the nations that rebelled more wickedly than they.
Unprecedented judgment for her abominations in the sight of the nations.
Fathers eating sons, the defiled sanctuary, God's pity withdrawn.

scenes.scene_name: A Third, a Third, a Third
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Plague, sword, and scattering — until God's wrath is spent.
Jerusalem made a ruin and a horror to the surrounding nations.
Famine, wild beasts, plague, and the sword sent against her.

scenes.scene_name: Set Your Face Against the Mountains
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The oracle to the mountains of Israel and their idolatrous high places.
The demolished altars and the scattered bones of the slain.

scenes.scene_name: Then You Will Know That I Am the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The cities laid waste, the idols smashed, the recognition formula.

scenes.scene_name: Yet I Will Leave a Remnant
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Survivors who, scattered among the nations, will loathe themselves and remember Him.

scenes.scene_name: Clap Your Hands, Stomp Your Feet
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The gesture of woe over abominations punished by sword, famine, and plague.

scenes.scene_name: A Desolate Waste from the Wilderness to Diblah
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The slain among their idols, the whole land made desolate.
The staccato 'end' upon the four corners of the land, judged without pity.
The unprecedented doom rousing itself against the inhabitants.

scenes.scene_name: I, the LORD, Who Strikes the Blow
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Wrath poured out and repaid according to their abominations.
Arrogance bloomed into violence, and none of the multitude will remain.
The futility of commerce when wrath is on the whole multitude.
The trumpet sounded in vain; sword without, plague and famine within.

scenes.scene_name: Moaning Like Doves of the Valley
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The survivors in sackcloth, every hand limp and every knee water.
Wealth become an unclean stumbling block, their idols made detestable.

scenes.scene_name: They Will Defile My Treasured Place
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Plunder to foreigners as God turns His face from the violated sanctuary.
The most wicked of nations brought to seize the violent, bloodstained land.

scenes.scene_name: They Will Seek a Vision, but Find None
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The failed prophet, priest, and elder; the king mourning in despair.

stories.story_title: The Temple Vision and the Glory Departing
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: A continuous vision: transported from Babylon to Jerusalem to witness the temple abominations, the marking and slaughter, and the stage-by-stage departure of the glory of the LORD. Start (8:1): the date and transport. End (11:25): return to the exiles. Glue: the moving kabod tracking the abandonment of the sanctuary, with the promise of a 'heart of flesh.'

scenes.scene_name: Transported to the Idol of Jealousy
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The sixth-year vision: carried by the hair to Jerusalem to see the glory and the provoking idol.
The idol of jealousy at the Altar Gate that drives God from His sanctuary.
The hidden doorway into the chamber of wicked abominations.
Crawling-creature idols and seventy censer-bearing elders — 'the LORD does not see us.'
The pagan mourning-rite at the north gate of the temple.
Twenty-five men with backs to the temple bowing east — 'I will respond with wrath.'

scenes.scene_name: The Executioners and the Man in Linen
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The six armed men summoned, with the scribe bearing a writing kit.

scenes.scene_name: Mark the Foreheads of Those Who Sigh
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The glory at the threshold; the mark set on those who grieve over the abominations.
The pitiless slaughter starting with the elders before the temple.
The prophet's cry, God's verdict on exceeding iniquity, and the scribe's report.
The sapphire throne and the command to scatter burning coals over the city.
The glory rising to the threshold amid the thunderous sound of the cherubim's wings.
The cherub handing fire to the man in linen, human hands beneath their wings.
The beryl wheels moving in any direction without turning.
Bodies full of eyes and the four faces of each cherub.

scenes.scene_name: The Living Creatures of the Kebar
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The cherubim recognized as the inaugural-vision creatures, the spirit in the wheels.
The kabod moving to stand at the east gate of the temple.
The explicit identification with the vision by the River Kebar.

scenes.scene_name: The City Is the Pot, We Are the Meat
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The twenty-five wicked counselors at the east gate and their false proverb of safety.
God reversing the proverb: the corpses they made are the meat, and He will remove them.

scenes.scene_name: Judged to the Borders of Israel
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The sword brought against them, delivered to foreigners.

scenes.scene_name: You Will Know That I Am the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The city no refuge-pot for those who followed the nations' ordinances.
Pelatiah's sudden death, the prophet's cry, and the scorn of those left in Jerusalem.
The promise to be a little sanctuary in exile and to regather them to the land.
The stony heart removed and a new spirit given — 'they will be My people.'
The kabod rising and standing over the mountain east of Jerusalem.
The Spirit returning Ezekiel to the exiles to report all he had seen.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: A cluster of sign-acts, disputations, and allegories on Jerusalem's certain fall: the exile-baggage, false prophets, the useless vine, the foundling bride (16), the two eagles (17), individual responsibility (18), and the lament for the princes (19). Glue: the discrediting of false hope and the parable/allegory form.

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The sign-act to a rebellious house with eyes that do not see.
Carrying the exile-baggage out at dusk, face covered, as a sign — and Ezekiel obeying.
The meaning for the prince in Jerusalem and all the house of Israel.
The prince taken to Babylon, which he will not see, and there die.
His attendants dispersed, a few spared to recount their abominations.
The second sign: anxious eating and drinking as the land is stripped by violence.
The end of the proverb 'every vision fails' — God's word delayed no longer.

scenes.scene_name: None of My Words Will Be Delayed
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Against those who push the vision off to the distant future.
Those who prophesy out of their own imagination, having seen nothing.
Prophets who did not repair the wall, seeing false visions.
The lying prophets cut from the register of the house of Israel.
The false 'peace' covered over a wall doomed to fall in the storm.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Tear Down the Wall
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The windstorm and hail leveling the whitewashed wall to its foundation.

scenes.scene_name: Peace Where There Was No Peace
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The end of the prophets who prophesied false peace to Jerusalem.

scenes.scene_name: The Women Who Sew Magic Charms
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The false prophetesses ensnaring souls for handfuls of barley.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Free the Ensnared Souls
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God tearing off their charms and veils to deliver His people.
Judgment for disheartening the righteous and encouraging the wicked.

scenes.scene_name: Idols Set Up in Their Hearts
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The inquiring elders whom God refuses to be consulted by.
God seizing the hearts of the idol-estranged.

scenes.scene_name: Repent and Turn from Your Idols
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The call to turn, and the cutting-off of the unrepentant idolater.
Both inquirer and deceived prophet bearing the same punishment.
Even these three could deliver only themselves from a sinning land's famine.
The same verdict under the judgment of beasts — only the righteous delivered.
The same under the sword: they could not save even their own children.
The same under plague — Noah, Daniel, and Job deliver only themselves.
Sword, famine, beasts, and plague on Jerusalem, yet survivors to bring consolation.
The parable of the useless vine-wood, fit only for fuel and charred.

scenes.scene_name: So I Will Give Up Jerusalem
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The vine-people handed to the fire, the land made desolate for unfaithfulness.

scenes.scene_name: Your Father an Amorite, Your Mother a Hittite
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The allegory of Jerusalem's pagan origins.

scenes.scene_name: Thrown Out in the Open Field
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The despised newborn left to die, uncared for on the day of her birth.
God passing by, giving life, and the foundling growing to beauty yet naked.

scenes.scene_name: I Entered into a Covenant with You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The spread cloak, the pledge, the washing — 'you became Mine.'

scenes.scene_name: Adorned with Jewelry and a Crown
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The lavish clothing, ornaments, and crown bestowed on her.
Her perfected beauty and fame spread among the nations.
Trusting in her beauty, prostituting herself to all who passed by.
Her gold and food turned into idols and pleasing offerings to them.
Child sacrifice to idols, forgetting the days of her bloody infancy.

scenes.scene_name: A Lofty Shrine at Every Street
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The escalating promiscuity that degraded her beauty.
Prostitution with lustful neighbors, never satisfied.
Extended to Chaldea, yet scorning the payment a harlot receives.
The reversal: bribing her lovers to come to her.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Expose You Before Your Lovers
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The gathering of all her lovers to see her nakedness.
Stripped and plundered, her shrines torn down.
Houses burned and judgment executed before many women.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Lay to Rest My Wrath
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God's jealousy turned away after bringing her deeds on her head.
Jerusalem the sister of Samaria and Sodom in her abominations.
Her sins surpassing even those of her sister cities.
Arrogant, overfed, and complacent, ignoring the poor and needy.

scenes.scene_name: You Made Your Sisters Appear Righteous
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Bearing her disgrace for sins more vile than Samaria's or Sodom's.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Restore Them, and You with Them
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The surprising promise to restore Sodom, Samaria, and Jerusalem.
Once-scornful Jerusalem now scorned by Edom and the Philistines.
God remembering the covenant of her youth despite her broken oath.
Her shamed silence when God atones for all she has done.

scenes.scene_name: The Great Eagle and the Cedar
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The riddle: an eagle plucking the cedar's top and carrying it to a land of traders.
The planted seed that grew into a vine bending toward the first eagle.
The vine stretching its roots toward another eagle for water.
The verdict that the east wind will wither the transplanted vine.
The interpretation: Nebuchadnezzar carrying off Judah's king and binding a vassal by oath.

scenes.scene_name: He Rebelled by Sending to Egypt
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The covenant-breaker who will die in Babylon for despising his oath.
The futility of Egypt's army against the siege; the broken pledge.
God bringing down on his head the despised oath, scattering his troops.

scenes.scene_name: A Tender Sprig on a Lofty Mountain
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The messianic promise: a cedar-shoot planted on Israel's heights sheltering every bird.

scenes.scene_name: The Soul Who Sins Will Die
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The end of the sour-grapes proverb: every soul belongs to God.
The portrait of the just man who keeps God's statutes.
The wicked son who will bear his own blood-guilt.
The son who sees his father's sins and turns from them.

scenes.scene_name: A Son Will Not Bear His Father's Guilt
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Each accountable for his own righteousness or wickedness.

scenes.scene_name: I Take No Pleasure in the Death of the Wicked
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The wicked who turns and lives — God preferring repentance to death.

scenes.scene_name: If a Righteous Man Turns Away
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The reversal: forsaken righteousness not remembered, against the charge 'the Lord is not just.'
The wicked who repents and saves his life — 'are My ways unjust?'

scenes.scene_name: Fashion a New Heart and Spirit
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The call to repent and live, for God takes no pleasure in anyone's death.
The lament for the princes: the first cub trapped and led to Egypt.
Another cub that devoured men and devastated cities.

scenes.scene_name: Brought to the King of Babylon
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The second lion caged and silenced on the mountains of Israel.

scenes.scene_name: A Vine Fit for a Ruler's Scepter
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The mother as a fruitful vine with strong, towering branches.
The vine cast down, dried by the east wind, consumed by fire — 'this is a lament.'

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: The rehearsal of Israel's rebellious history (20), the sword song (21), the bloody city's sins (22), the allegory of Oholah and Oholibah (23), and the boiling pot with the death of Ezekiel's wife as a sign (24), which seals the first half as Jerusalem falls. Glue: the lawsuit of accumulated guilt reaching its terminus.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Not Be Consulted by You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The seventh-year inquiry refused as the elders sit before the prophet.

scenes.scene_name: I Swore an Oath in Egypt
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God's self-revelation to Jacob's house — 'I am the LORD your God.'
Their clinging to Egypt's idols, yet God acting for His name's sake.
The statutes given in the wilderness and the Sabbath sanctifying-sign.
The profaned Sabbaths met by mercy for the sake of God's name.

scenes.scene_name: I Swore Not to Bring Them In
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The oath barring that generation, yet God's restraining pity.

scenes.scene_name: Do Not Walk in Your Fathers' Statutes
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The charge to the next generation to keep God's ordinances and Sabbaths.
The second generation's rebellion and God's withheld hand.
The oath to scatter them, given over to ruinous practices.
The high-place worship in the land — the shrine named Bamah.

scenes.scene_name: Will You Defile Yourselves Like Them?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The continuing child-sacrifice idolatry — 'I will not be consulted.'
The wish to be like the nations thwarted by God's mighty hand.
A new exodus into face-to-face judgment as with the fathers.
The covenant-bond, with the rebels purged from entering the land.

scenes.scene_name: On My Holy Mountain They Will Serve Me
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The ironic 'go serve your idols,' then the promise of true worship on Zion.
God's holiness shown through the regathered people brought into the land.
The shame of remembered sin, God dealing with them for His name's sake.

scenes.scene_name: A Fire in the Forest of the Negev
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The oracle to the south: an unquenchable flame scorching every face.

scenes.scene_name: Is He Not Just Telling Parables?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The people's dismissal of the prophet's vivid imagery.
The oracle against Jerusalem cutting off both righteous and wicked.
The unsheathed sword against everyone from south to north.
The prophet's sign-groan over the news that makes every heart melt.
The polished blade flashing like lightning for the slaughter.
The sword in the slayer's hand against the princes of Israel.

scenes.scene_name: Let the Sword Strike Two, Even Three
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The great slaughter closing in on every side.
The sword appointed at every gate, God striking His hands together.

scenes.scene_name: Two Roads for the Sword of Babylon
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The signpost marking the routes to Rabbah and to Jerusalem.

scenes.scene_name: The King at the Fork in the Road
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Nebuchadnezzar's divination pointing the omen toward Jerusalem.

scenes.scene_name: You Shall Be Taken in Hand
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The exposed guilt of those who break their sworn allegiance.
The profane prince deposed — a ruin 'until He comes to whom it belongs.'
The drawn sword for their contempt, placed on the necks of the slain.

scenes.scene_name: You Will Be Fuel for the Fire
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The sword returned to judge Ammon in the land of its origin.
The summons to judge the city full of blood and idols.

scenes.scene_name: You Have Brought Your Days to a Close
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The self-doomed city made a reproach to all lands.
The catalog of sins: oppressed orphan and widow, despised Sabbaths.
Slander, incest, and indecency among her people.
Bribery and extortion answered by God's striking hands.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Scatter You Among the Nations
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The purging dispersal by which they will know the LORD.
The house of Israel as worthless metal in the furnace.
God gathering them into Jerusalem to melt them in His wrath.
The land on which no cleansing rain has fallen in the day of wrath.
The devouring leaders and the priests who profane God's holy things.
The dishonest officials and the whitewashing false prophets.

scenes.scene_name: I Found No One to Stand in the Gap
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The searched-for intercessor not found, so wrath is poured out.
The two sisters — Samaria and Jerusalem — who prostituted themselves from youth.
Samaria's prostitution with the Assyrian warriors and their idols.
Samaria exposed and put to the sword, a byword among women.
Jerusalem outdoing her sister, lusting after the same Assyrians.

scenes.scene_name: Lust for the Chaldeans on the Wall
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Jerusalem sending for the Babylonians she saw portrayed in vermilion.
Defiled by the Babylonians, then loathing them as God loathed her.
Multiplied promiscuity recalling her lewd youth in Egypt.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Incite Your Lovers Against You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The Babylonians and Chaldeans brought against her on every side.

scenes.scene_name: They Will Cut Off Your Nose and Ears
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The fury of mutilation and the stripping of her finery.
An end to her Egypt-rooted indecency, delivered to those she hates.

scenes.scene_name: You Will Drink Your Sister's Cup
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The deep, wide cup of scorn passed from Samaria to Jerusalem.
The cup of desolation drained, for forgetting God and casting Him behind her back.
The sisters' adultery, child-sacrifice, and profaned Sabbaths.

scenes.scene_name: They Entered My Sanctuary to Profane It
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Child-slaughter followed by temple-defilement and the couch of luxury.
The carefree crowd and the men who slept with the lewd sisters.
The mob bringing the adulteresses' judgment of stoning and fire.

scenes.scene_name: An End to Indecency in the Land
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The warning to all women, and the recognition formula.
The very day the king of Babylon laid siege to Jerusalem.

scenes.scene_name: Put the Pot on the Fire
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The parable of the boiling cauldron filled with choice meat and bones.

scenes.scene_name: The Pot Whose Rust Will Not Come Off
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Woe to the bloody city whose unburied blood cries for vengeance.
The empty pot heated until its copper glows and its impurity melts.

scenes.scene_name: Its Rust Not Removed Even by Fire
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The uncleanness God's wrath alone can purge — 'I will not relent.'

scenes.scene_name: The Desire of Your Eyes Taken
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The command not to mourn the coming death of Ezekiel's wife.
The sign performed, and the people's question of its meaning.
The temple, the desire of their eyes, to be profaned and their children to fall.
The exiles to mourn silently as he did when the news comes.
The promise that the fugitive's report will end the prophet's muteness.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: The transitional judgments on the surrounding nations — Ammon, Moab, Edom, Philistia (25), Tyre (26-28), and Egypt (29-32) — demonstrating the LORD's universal sovereignty. Glue: the nation-by-nation oracle formula and the recurring recognition formula.

stories.story_title: Watchman Renewed: Shepherds, Dry Bones, and Gog
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: The hinge to restoration: the watchman recommissioned and the fall of Jerusalem reported (33), the worthless shepherds and the true Shepherd (34), judgment on Edom (35), the renewed land and new heart (36), the valley of dry bones and the two sticks (37), and the defeat of Gog of Magog (38-39). Glue: the turn from death to resurrection and from scattering to regathering.

stories.story_title: The Vision of the New Temple
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: The climactic vision of the restored temple: its measurements (40-42), the return of the glory of the LORD (43), the priestly and worship ordinances (44-46), the life-giving river from the temple (47), and the new allotment of the land, ending with the city's name 'The LORD Is There' (48:35). Glue: the merkabah returning, completing the book's inclusio.
